source_evidence: The fund then pays the shareholders nearly all the income, less expenses, as a dividend payment.
answer: A mutual fund may earn income from investments in its portfolio, such as stock dividends or bond interest. It pays shareholders nearly all of that income, after expenses, as dividend payments. You may receive the payment or, if the fund offers the choice, reinvest it to buy more shares. Dividend or interest payments can change as market conditions change.
